name: Stretch Bench
description: A machinist's setting-out bench for scalar multiplication k*v. One amber reference arrow v is clamped to a graduated brass rail; turn the single brass 'k' crank (it physically slides along the rail, so the scalar's POSITION on the number line IS the input) and a twin arrow grows, shrinks, collapses to a glowing dot at k=0, and flips 180 degrees through its own tail when k goes negative. The twin reads cyan-violet for k>=0 and RED when reversed. k*v and |k*v|=|k|*|v| tick live the whole way. A SNAP button locks k to integers so you can land exactly on k=-1 (mirror) and k=2 (double). slider_horizontal stays wired as the desktop fallback.
theoreticalGrounding: To multiply a vector by a number is to choose a length and a direction-sign on a line you have already drawn. Scalar multiplication never touches the line's direction — only its magnitude and sign. |k*v| = |k|*|v|, always; negative k is reversal, k=0 is collapse, |k|>1 is stretch.

stretch_bench.name: Stretch Bench
stretch_bench.description: Dark slate pedestal + brass rim + graduated rail (the number line for k). A grabbable brass crank slides along the rail to set k in [-3,+3]; the amber base vector v is grabbable (re-aim the reference line), the derived twin k*v snaps to it and is never grabbable — cyan-violet when k>=0, red when k<0, a glowing dot at k=0. Etched integer ground-lattice (-3v..3v), a bead + brass 'k' dial needle, live k*v and |k||v| readout, SNAP integer-lock button, and a slider_horizontal desktop fallback. DNA: default_k, min_k, max_k, base_vector.
stretch_bench.qfep_connection: F_field / scalar: one number reshapes one vector — length and sign on a fixed line. k<0 reverses, k=0 collapses, |k|>1 stretches; the twin is the field-value of v under the scalar.

dna.default: regime=identity, workings=expression - identity SHORT-CIRCUITS: _regime_k() hands back the shipped default_k rather than the table's 1.0, so a map that overrides k alone opens at its own number instead of being reset to the regime's. At k=1 the twin is positioned by the same _refresh_geometry call over the same base_vector, in twin_color and not twin_flip_color, with the collapse dot hidden, the crank and bead at _k_to_rail_x(1.0) and the needle at lerp(-120,120,0.667) - the literals that were there before. expression turns every gate on, which is the only state this bench could previously be in: the etched -3v..3v lattice with its ticks and ghost labels, the bead, the amber grabbable v, the brass crank, the k dial and the two-column info panel. All 3 placements (Force_Preview, MiniScene_stretch_bench, VFM_01_Foundations) are BARE tokens with no #key:value, and both axes are read only inside `if config.has(...)`, so none of them reaches the new code. Nothing in apply_grid_config tears anything down on any path: regime moves a number _refresh_all already reads, workings is visibility on nodes already standing.
dna.was: no @export at all, which is why the stage-2 runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. default_k, min_k, max_k, base_vector and housed were plain vars reachable through apply_grid_config - real knobs, but a range, two bounds, a direction and a cabinet flag, and not one of them an argument. The bench's whole content is what k DOES to a vector, and this file names the cases four times in prose (the @identity's 'k=+1 identity, k=0 collapse, k=-1 perfect mirror ... the three landmarks are the whole lesson', the panel's 'k<0 reverses / k=0 collapses', the red twin_flip_color, _refresh_text's REVERSED/COLLAPSED/same way) while a placed bench could only ever stand at k=1 until a player turned the crank. The scaffolding had the same problem in the other direction: the ghost lattice, the operand, the dial and the panel were hard-wired to go up together, so a room could not show a scaled vector as a bare result.
dna.shared_with: workings is length_lantern's word with its four values in the same order - the honest test of the vocabulary here, because length_lantern is the HOUSING sibling (same dark slate plinth, same brass rim, same etched integer lattice) and stands beside this bench in Force_Preview's row with adder_board and agreement_gauge. Seconded by adder_board, vector_add, vector_sub, dot_aligner, projection_shadow and transform_composition_workbench. `regime` is the corpus's word for which named case of a governing scalar is on display (bouncing_ball, rotation_gimbal, homogeneous_coordinates, VectorForces); the values are this bench's own, DERIVED from its four in-file namings of the cases rather than borrowed, because a damping ladder has no identity rung and scalar multiplication has no critical one.
dna.note: The rail genuinely reaches every declared regime, checked in the code and not assumed: the lattice loop etches a tick and a ghost label at every integer from min_k=-3 to max_k=3, and _k_to_rail_x maps the full range onto RAIL_HALF_LEN, so k=-1 is a real position (x=-0.4) with a '-v' label under it. dot_aligner and bounce_well both once promised cases their controls could not produce; this one can.
